text.text_excerpt: 4/5 ok, I can be into it so maybe this is swayed by the fact that I love Filipino food, and maybe that fact is swayed by the fact that I'm Filipino and grew up eating all this yumminess, so you know, take that into consideration. i had heard of milkfish since before i moved to nola a year ago. i had panics in the deepest, fattiest part of my heart. it wondered - where will i find filipino food?! and then i heard of this place, and now you've heard of this place, and folks nationally have too (they were featured in DETAILS). i failed to find them last fall, it's hard to keep up with food trucks and popups in nola, for some reason just not as easy as it was back in the bay. right now they'r...

I am pretty sure this is the only Filipino place in NOLA, so there's that. The food was awesome. I really liked it. No clue if it was legit or not but it was different than the normal NOLA cuisine. I got the sigigi which was great. it has liver in it and I dont think I knew that before hand. Very good but it can shock you if you arent ready for the liver. Really good though. Also got something with ox tail in it. it is 85% bone and annoying to get off. tasted really good but too much effort for too little of meat. tasted really good but I wouldnt get it again. They dont have a liscense so it is byob. no big deal. good place. i would recommend it for sure because it is so different than yo...

Came here on a Sunday night when it seems like a majority of the restaurants in the area is closed. It was their last weekend at the pop up location at A Mano a Italian restaurant. There's currently a big surge in popularity of Pilipino food in NYC and I wanted to check out New Orleans take on it. This being a pop up space, it was a bit bare with shoe string staff and borrowed art, but the service overall was friendly and helpful. It was also quite exciting that many of the patrons that stopped by was Philipino.
